text:
Aisha: FYI Smaug POC reporting 429s during initial SDK onboarding ramp, started after they ran CI smoke that parallelized requests x50 against our preflight
Sam: ok looking into it now, can you paste the exact client behavior?
Aisha: they rotate ephemeral tokens per request and call /v1/embedded/preflight for every session. sample from their repro: `for i in range(50): fetch('/preflight', {headers: {Authorization: token()}})`
Miguel: that pattern will hit the preflight auth window hard — we recommend session reuse + limited preflight concurrency
Aisha: Smaug POC says security requires per-request tokens, they asked if we can help with server-side suggestions or a temporary quota relief
Sam: short term: enable short-lived session tokens (1–2m) instead of per-request, or add a token cache on their gateway. Also add jittered backoff on 429s. Example patch for Node SDK: `opts.preflightConcurrency = 3` and `opts.ephemeralCacheMs = 60000`
Miguel: also send them our recommended header to correlate: `X-RW-Client: smaug-ci` and `X-RW-ReqID` so we can trace bursts
Aisha: forwarding plan to POC now. Also opened a support ticket and asked infra for a transient quota bump while they adopt changes — @cs-bot can you confirm ticket ID?
cs-bot: created ticket CS-1234: "Smaug onboarding preflight surge" assigned to infra-oncall
Smaug POC: thanks! we'll try the session cache and report back in ~30m
Sam: if they still hit 429s after session reuse, we'll capture headers/traces and consider a short-term burst window on their account. Suggested client changes: reduce parallel preflight to <=5, reuse ephemeral tokens for 60s, and add exponential backoff with full jitter
Aisha: noted, follow-up scheduled after their deploy. leaving breadcrumbs here for runbook update. :thumbsup:
